label: Erdős 1946 main theorem
statement_text: Main theorem of Erdős 1946: U(n) ≥ c · n^{1 + c'/log log n} for some absolute constants c, c' > 0. Proof outline: take the integer grid Z² ∩ [0, √n]² (which has n points), compute all pairwise distances-squared, observe that these are sums of two squares, then apply Landau-style multiplicative bounds on r₂(k) (the number of representations of k as a²+b²) to extract a frequent distance whose multiplicity is Ω(n / (log n)^{1 - log 2}). Scaling the grid so that frequent distance becomes 1 yields the claimed unit-distance count.
description: Updated in Loop 5 with real proof content. IsLoadBearing flipped from false to true; this IS what supports the Erdős bound.
name: erdős-1946-main-theorem

label: Sum-of-two-squares representation count r₂(k)
statement_text: Number-theoretic fact (Landau, Hardy–Wright): the representation function r₂(k) = #{(a,b) ∈ Z² : a²+b² = k} is multiplicative; for k = 2^a · ∏ p_i^{α_i} · ∏ q_j^{β_j} with p_i ≡ 1 (mod 4) and q_j ≡ 3 (mod 4), r₂(k) = 4 · ∏(α_i+1) if all β_j even, else 0. For k = product of t primes ≡ 1 (mod 4), r₂(k) = 4 · 2^t. Choosing k with t ~ log log n gives r₂(k) ~ (log n)^{log 2}, the multiplicity needed for Erdős's bound.
description: NEW in Loop 5. The number-theoretic supporting lemma — Erdős's bound rides on this multiplicative structure of r₂(k). Cited in 1946 to Landau; FeedsObject is the grid-construction lemma above (lemma chain: divisor-function → grid-construction → main-theorem).
name: sum-of-two-squares-representation-count-r₂(k)

label: Integer-grid pigeonhole construction
statement_text: Let G_n = Z² ∩ [0, √n]² be the √n × √n integer-grid point set; |G_n| ≈ n. For any pair (p, q) ∈ G_n × G_n, |p - q|² ∈ Z. The multiset of pairwise squared distances is concentrated: the integer k = a² + b² appears Θ(n · r₂(k)/k) times among pairs at squared-distance k (where r₂ counts representations). For k = m² · ∏ p_i with p_i ≡ 1 (mod 4), r₂(k) grows; choosing k with r₂(k) = Ω((log n)^{log 2}) gives a single squared-distance achieved Ω(n^{1+c/loglogn}) times.
description: NEW in Loop 5. The 'grid → distance histogram' step of Erdős's proof. The integer-distance restriction is what makes pigeonhole work — distances on a real-coordinate point set don't concentrate, integer-grid distances do.
name: integer-grid-pigeonhole-construction

label: Crossing number inequality (ACNS 1982)
statement_text: Ajtai–Chvátal–Newborn–Szemerédi 1982: any drawing of a graph G with n vertices and m ≥ 4n edges in the plane has at least c · m³/n² crossings (for some absolute constant c > 0). The Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter unit-distance upper bound U(n) = O(n^{4/3}) follows from applying this to the unit-distance graph drawn with arcs.
description: NEW in Loop 5. The crossing-number-inequality lemma that powers the upper-bound side of the sandwich on U(n). Real content from training, not placeholder.
